'''Sybren Otto''' (Groningen, 3 August 1971) is [[Professor]] of [[Systems chemistry]] at the [[Stratingh Institute for Chemistry]], [[University of Groningen]].

== Career ==
Otto studied [[chemistry]] at the University of Groningen and in 1994, he received his [[Master's degree]], focusing on [[physical organic chemistry]] and [[biochemistry]], with the distinction [[cum laude]]. In 1998, he obtained his [[PhD]], again with the distinction cum laude, from his supervisor Prof. Jan B.F.N. Engberts for his [[thesis]] entitled Catalysis of Diels-Alder reactions in water.

After his subsequent [[research]] in both the [[United States]] (in 1998, with Prof. Steven L. Regen) at [[Lehigh University]] and in the [[United Kingdom]] (first with [[Jeremy Sanders|Prof. Jeremy K.M. Sanders]] and then, from 2001 onwards, as a [[Royal Society University Research Fellow]], both at the [[University of Cambridge]]), he was appointed [[assistant professor]] at the University of Groningen in 2009. In 2011, he was promoted to [[associate professor]] and in 2016, to [[full professor]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0259-5637|title=sijbren otto, employment|language= en|publisher=ORCID |access-date=12 November 2019}}</ref> From 2014 to 2019, he coordinated the master's degree programme in chemistry.

Alongside his work at the university, Otto is also one of the six principal investigators of the Dutch ''national gravity programme for functional molecular systems'' (FMS; €26 million, over 10 years, 2013–2023).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nwo.nl/actueel/nieuws/2012/rijk-investeert-167-miljoen-in-nederlands-toponderzoek.html|title=rijk investeert 167 miljoen in nederlands toponderzoek|language=nl |publisher=NWO|date=14 November 2012 |access-date=13 November 2019}}</ref> The ambition of this programme is to gain control over molecular [[self-assembly]]. With this technology, [[nanomotors]] could be made, for example, or [[biomaterials]] to repair damaged bodily [[Tissue (biology)|tissues]].
Otto was the lead applicant and chair of the European Cooperation in Science & Technology (COST) Action CM1304 (Emergence and Evolution of Complex Chemical Systems), which united more than 95 European research groups.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.cost.eu/actions/CM1304/www.systemschemistry.com/cm1304/#tabs|title= action leadership positions|publisher= EU|access-date= 14 November 2019}}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> He is the chair of the [[Gordon Research Conference]] on Systems Chemistry 2020 <ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.grc.org/systems-chemistry-conference/2020/|title= Systems Chemistry Gordon Research Conference|publisher= CGR|access-date= 14 November 2019|archive-date= 13 November 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191113170953/https://www.grc.org/systems-chemistry-conference/2020/|url-status= dead}}</ref> and is [[editor-in-chief]] of the ''Journal of Systems Chemistry''.<ref>{{cite journal|title= Welcome Home, Systems Chemists!|publisher= Springer|date= 18 August 2010 |doi= 10.1186/1759-2208-1-1|last1= von Kiedrowski|first1= Günter|last2= Otto|first2= Sijbren|last3= Herdewijn|first3= Piet|journal= Journal of Systems Chemistry|volume= 1|article-number= 1|doi-access= free|hdl= 11370/28ddfb30-005b-4724-b67b-0ce7a4f07136|hdl-access= free}}</ref>

Otto is a member of the [[Royal Dutch Chemical Society]] (KNCV),  fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] and member of the [[American Chemical Society]]. He is member of the steering committee of the Origins Center.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.origins-center.nl/people/|title= People|publisher= Origins|access-date= 6 December 2019|archive-date= 5 August 2020|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20200805224858/https://www.origins-center.nl/people/|url-status= dead}}</ref> The Origins Center is a Dutch research platform for scientists who are involved in the key questions of the Dutch Research Agenda on the origin, evolution and future of life on Earth and in the universe.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.origins-center.nl|title= What is the Origins Center|publisher=Origins Center |access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref> Otto is active on several fronts in both the Netherlands and abroad.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.otto-lab.com/ExtendedCV%20SijbrenOtto.pdf|title= Sijbren Otto|publisher= Otto Research Group|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref> Otto was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/16604 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502085824/https://knaw.nl/en/members/members/16604 |title=Sijbren Otto |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |archive-date=2 May 2020}}</ref>

== Research ==
The research conducted by Otto and his research group is focused on various fields, varying from the origin of life ([[Self-replication|self-replicating systems]] and the [[Darwinism|Darwinian evolution thereof]]), to [[materials chemistry]] (self-[[Chemical synthesis|synthesizing]] [[fibres]], [[hydrogels]] and [[nanoparticle]] surfaces).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.otto-lab.com/research.htm|title= research |publisher= Otto Research Group |access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref>

Specific interests include [[Self-replication|self-replicating]] [[molecules]], [[foldamers]], [[catalysis]], molecular recognition of biomolecules and self-synthesizing materials (materials of which their self-assembly drives the synthesis of the molecules that assemble). The complex chemical mixtures that are designed, made and researched often display new properties that are relevant to understanding how new traits are able to arise in nature. The final goal of all of this research is the [[de novo synthesis]] of new forms of life via the integration of self-replicating systems with [[metabolism]] and [[Cellular compartment|compartmentalization]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rug.nl/staff/s.otto/research|title= Results|publisher= RUG|access-date= 13 November 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.volkskrant.nl/wetenschap/mogelijke-voorloper-van-leven-op-aarde-duikt-op-in-gronings-lab~b82cb0a8/|title= Mogelijke voorloper van leven op aarde duikt op in Gronings lab Results| date=5 January 2016 |language= nl |publisher= De Volkskrant|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref> His 114 publications have been cited a total of 8,873 times by other scientists. His [[h-index]] is 51.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7101616525 |title=Author details S. Otto |publisher= Elsevier|access-date= 27 November 2019}}</ref>

* 1999 [[Marie Curie Fellowship]], [[University of Cambridge]], United Kingdom.
* 2000 Junior Research Fellowship, [[Wolfson College, Cambridge]], United Kingdom.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.admin.cam.ac.uk/reporter/2000-01/weekly/5832/44.html|title= Wolfson College|publisher= UoC|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref>
* 2001 [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]], University of Cambridge, United Kingdom.
* 2011 [[ERC Starting Grant]] (subsidy) from the [[European Research Council]] for research into: ''Self-replication in dynamic molecular networks''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://erc.europa.eu/sites/default/files/document/file/erc_2011_stg_results_all_domains.pdf|title=ERC Starting Grants 2011 |publisher= European Union|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref>
* 2013 Vici grant from the Dutch Research Council (NWO) for research into: ''the Darwinian evolution of molecules''.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nwo.nl/onderzoek-en-resultaten/programmas/vernieuwingsimpuls/toekenningen/alle+vici+toekenningen/Toekenningen+Vici+2012|title= Toekenningen Vici 2012|language= nl|publisher= NWO|access-date= 14 November 2019|archive-date= 14 October 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191014212759/https://www.nwo.nl/onderzoek-en-resultaten/programmas/vernieuwingsimpuls/toekenningen/alle%20vici%20toekenningen/Toekenningen%20Vici%202012|url-status= dead}}</ref> (Vici grants are intended for excellent senior researchers who can demonstrably develop their own innovative research lines and who are suitable for coaching early-career researchers.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/Talent+Scheme/awards/vici+awards|title= VICI Awards|language= nl|publisher= NWO|access-date= 19 November 2019|archive-date= 14 December 2019|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191214125056/https://www.nwo.nl/en/research-and-results/programmes/Talent%2BScheme/awards/vici%2Bawards|url-status= dead}}</ref>
* 2013 Appointed as Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://pubs.rsc.org/en/results?searchtext=Author%3ASijbren%20Otto|title= ERC Starting Grants 2011|language= nl |publisher= RSC|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref>
* 2013 [[Visiting professor]], [[University of Strasbourg]], [[France]].
* 2017 [[ERC Advanced Grant]] (subsidy) from the European Research Council.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://erc.europa.eu/projects-figures/erc-funded-projects/results?search_api_views_fulltext=sijbren+otto |title=erc funded projects |publisher=ERC |access-date=14 November 2019 }}{{Dead link|date=December 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.rug.nl/news/2017/03/two-erc-advanced-grants-for-ug-scientists|title=Twee ERC Advanced Grants voor RUG-onderzoekers|date=29 March 2017 |language= nl |publisher= RUG|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref>
* 2018 Visiting professor, [[LMU Munich]], Germany.
* 2018 Supramolecular chemistry prize of the Royal Society of Chemistry.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/SupramolecularChemistryAward/2018-Winner.asp|title=2018 Supramolecular Chemistry Award Winner|publisher= RSC|access-date= 14 November 2019}}</ref>
* 2020 Member of the [[Royal_Netherlands_Academy_of_Arts_and_Sciences|Royal Dutch Academy of Science]] ([https://knaw.nl/en/news/news/royal-academy-selects-eighteen-new-members link]).
* 2023 [[ERC Synergy Grant]] (subsidy) from the European Research Council. <ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rug.nl/fse/news/2023/drie-erc-synergy-grants-voor-groningse-onderzoekers|title = Three ERC Synergy grants for Groningen researchers| date=26 October 2023 |language= en |publisher= RUG|access-date= 20 November 2023}}</ref>
